quarterly_data.signal: 10-K fiscal 2025 results: total revenues were $255,869 thousand (+23% from $207,539 thousand); software products and services revenue was $199,500 thousand (+11%) and drug discovery revenue $56,369 thousand (+107% from $27,174 thousand). Within software, hosted software revenue grew 28% to $45,123 thousand while on-premise software fell 2% to $101,448 thousand; software gross margin was 74% versus 80% in 2024. Sales to customers outside the United States were approximately 40% of total revenues.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenue $255,869 thousand (+23%); software $199,500 thousand (+11%); drug discovery $56,369 thousand (+107%); hosted software $45,123 thousand (+28%); on-premise $101,448 thousand (-2%); software gross margin 74% (80%)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K software customer metrics for 2025: all of the top 20 pharmaceutical companies (by 2024 revenue) licensed Schrödinger's solutions, accounting for $73.7 million, or 37%, of software revenue and $80.8 million, or 41%, of annual contract value (ACV). There were 27 commercial customers with ACV of at least $1.0 million (29 in 2024), and their average ACV grew to $3.9 million from $3.3 million. Gross dollar retention for commercial customers was 96% in both 2025 and 2024; net dollar retention was 100% versus 113%.
quarterly_data.figure: top 20 pharma: $73.7 million (37% of software revenue), $80.8 million (41% of ACV); 27 customers with ACV of at least $1.0 million (29); average ACV $3.9 million ($3.3 million); gross retention 96%; net retention 100% (113%)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K customer concentration (customer not named): one customer accounted for 17% of total revenues in 2025 and 10% in 2024; in 2023 two customers accounted for 26% and 11%. At December 31, 2025 three customers accounted for 21%, 12% and 10% of contract assets. The 10-K names its current drug discovery collaborators as including Ajax Therapeutics, BMS, Bright Angel Therapeutics, Lilly, Novartis, Otsuka Pharmaceutical, Sanofi and Structure Therapeutics; collaboration agreements typically include upfront consideration, discovery, development, commercial and regulatory milestones, and royalties.
